question: How are ha, ṣa, kṣa, and the group ending with ma placed on the breath and lower body?
premises: The letter ha is declared to be the vital breath.
The letters ṣa and kṣa are placed on the belly and the navel.
The group ending with ma goes to the hips, private parts, and pair of thighs, and likewise to the two knees.
inference: Verse 124 completes the lower-body mapping of the Mālinī nyāsa from the vital breath down to the knees.
uncertainties: The exact members of 'maśāntā' depend on the Mālinī sequence and are not individually listed in this verse.
The distribution of that group across hips, private parts, thighs, and knees is stated collectively rather than one-to-one.
plain_english: Ha is declared to be the vital breath. Ṣa and kṣa go to the belly and the navel. The group ending with ma goes to the hips, the private parts, and the pair of thighs, and likewise to the two knees.
